ai.title: Progress-focused collapsed preview for editor-multi-prompt
ai.summary: Replaced separate streaming/finished preview props with a unified `preview` prop in `AgentBranchItem` and `AgentBranchWrapper`. Added logic in `implementor-helpers.ts` to detect `editor-multi-prompt` agents via `constants.ts` and generate progress-focused previews (e.g., "2/3 completed", "selecting best") or extract selection reasons from `set_output`. Implemented `truncateToLines` in `strings.ts` to limit collapsed previews to `MAX_COLLAPSED_LINES` (3). Updated `editor-multi-prompt.ts` to include `reason` in `set_output` input.

eli5.text: When a multi-step editing task is running and you've collapsed its branch in the CLI, you now see a short progress summary instead of a generic preview line. The system counts how many sub-tasks finished or failed and, depending on the phase, shows text like '2/3 completed' while they run and 'selecting best' when it's choosing the final result; once done, it surfaces the reason the chosen approach was picked. This preview is trimmed to three lines max, and the editor now records that reason in its output so it can be shown to you. Live today.

ai.title: Remove 120-character width cap in CLI terminal display
ai.summary: The hardcoded 120-character width limit in terminal command display is removed, allowing output to expand to the full available content width. This change is made in `cli/src/components/terminal-command-display.tsx` to prevent unnecessary truncation of long commands or outputs in wide terminals.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the CLI and the terminal window is wide, the assistant will no longer shrink-wrap long command or output lines to 120 characters; it now spreads them across the full available width, so wide-screen displays show complete, untruncated text. The previous 120-character ceiling was removed by adjusting how the terminal display calculates its width, letting the visible content match whatever horizontal space your terminal window provides. This only affects terminal output, so any line that previously wrapped or got cut off at 120 columns should now extend farther across the screen instead. You don't need to turn anything on for this to take effect.

ai.title: Read-subtree now accepts paths with trailing slashes
ai.summary: `handleReadSubtree` strips trailing slashes from input paths before resolution. This prevents failures when users pass directories like `src/` instead of `src`. Change is scoped to `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/read-subtree.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to read a folder, you can now type the name with a trailing slash at the end, like 'src/' instead of just 'src', and it will still work correctly. Previously, the extra slash would cause the request to fail unexpectedly. This small fix simply ignores any extra slashes you add to the end of a folder path before processing it.

ai.title: Reorder hero subtitle to prioritize quality
ai.summary: The `Hero` component subtitle in `web/src/components/ui/hero.tsx` is reordered to place 'Higher quality output' before the speed comparison. This change adjusts the visual hierarchy of the landing page messaging. The modification affects only the web UI component.

eli5.text: When you open the website today, the welcome message now leads with better output quality before mentioning that the assistant is faster than other tools. The text about speed and quality was swapped in order, so 'Higher quality output and 100+ seconds faster than Claude Code' now reads quality-first instead of speed-first. This affects what you see on the landing page only.

ai.title: spawnagents tool misuse error
ai.summary: Added check in validateAndGetAgentTemplate to detect when a tool name is passed as agentTypeStr. Throws specific error instructing direct tool invocation instead of wrapping in spawn_agents. Affects packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-utils.ts.

eli5.text: If you tried to start a helper by typing its name into the special 'create helper' box, you now get a clear message telling you to type that name directly as a command instead. The system checks the name you gave and, if it matches a known helper, stops you with step-by-step instructions on how to use it properly, rather than a confusing failure.

ai.title: GLM editor agent uses high reasoning effort
ai.summary: The code editor agent now sets `reasoningOptions.effort: 'high'` when `model` is 'glm'. This aligns the editor's behavior with high-reasoning requirements for GLM in free mode. Scope limited to `agents/editor/editor.ts`. The change conditionally applies the reasoning config via spread syntax only for the GLM model variant.

eli5.text: When you open the built-in code editor and pick the GLM model, it will now think harder before acting, trading a bit of speed for more careful, well-reasoned output. This mainly matters if you're using the editor on the free tier with the GLM model selected, rather than the default options. You won't see anything flashy - the only visible difference is that the editor may take slightly longer before producing its first edit when GLM is your chosen model. The change is live today and only affects the specific case of the GLM model being used in the editor.

ai.title: Update what-models docs
ai.summary: Models documentation updated to reflect current agent configuration. `Lite` mode renamed to `Free`, and subagent model assignments changed (e.g., `GLM 4.7` for editing, `GPT-5.2` for reasoning). Scope limited to `web/src/content/advanced/what-models.mdx`.

eli5.text: The guide explaining which AI models power different helper agents got updated. The 'Lite' mode people can pick is now called 'Free', and the specific assistants that handle coding, thinking, file searches, terminal work, and web research have each been swapped out for different model versions. If you open that guide, you'll see the updated table of which helper uses which model, and the description of what the Free mode does differently. None of this changes what you can click on today, but it clarifies what's happening behind the scenes.

ai.title: Add tool error handling to stream parser
ai.summary: Added error handling for tool calls in `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/stream-parser.ts`. If a tool call returns an error, the system now flags `hadToolCallError` and appends a user message with the error details and retry instructions. State variables moved outside the stream consumption loop to ensure errors are captured correctly.

eli5.text: When a tool the assistant uses fails mid-conversation, the assistant now keeps going and hands you a clear error note plus retry steps instead of stopping or losing the error detail. The fix catches tool failures during the streaming response and appends them as a new message you can read and act on. This is live today for anyone running the agent runtime.
